Ingrid: Quick recap from today's all-hands Q&A on release cadence, oncall, quality bars, and SLAs. Posting short answers and next steps.

Lee: Nice, can you confirm the cadence?

Ingrid: Biweekly release train (Tue 09:00 PT) for major work, weekly (Thu) for minor infra patches, and hotfixes ad-hoc via the rollback playbook. Feature work should be gated by flags when possible.

Sofia: Oncall notes: 2-week rotations, primary + secondary. Escalation: primary -> secondary -> oncall manager (20m) -> SRE lead. Targets: acknowledge within 10m, attempt mitigation/rollback within 30m. If hosted SLA might be affected, notify CS within 1h.

Lee: Are Dedicated/enterprise customers on the same pager SLOs?

Sofia: Default internal SLO is 10m. Dedicated enterprise SLAs can be tighter per SOW; sales should reference the customer's contract.

Priya: Canary defaults for model rollouts: 5% for 1h, 25% for 6h, then full if green. Monitor: model-quality evals, token-error rate, user error-rate, latency p95/p99. Auto-rollback triggers include: quality drop >5% on labeled evals, user error rate >2x baseline, or p99 latency +40% (or p95 +200ms) over baseline. ML will tune thresholds per model.

Lee: Where do we keep the playbooks?

DevBot: Release playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/release-cadence  Canary policy: https://redwood.internal/platform/canary-policy  Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-response

Ingrid: We're scheduling a 45-min office hours next Wed 4pm PT to walk the playbook and take deeper Qs. Priya will update the playbook with canary numbers and a RACI by EOD Friday. Sofia will post the oncall rota template after office hours. Tag me here with anything missing.
